title: Sell Mineral Rights in Friendsville, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Friendsville, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Friendsville, Susquehanna County? Dry-gas Marcellus territory near the New York line. We buy oil and gas interests — no pressure.
heroLead: Friendsville sits close enough to the New York state line that some Susquehanna County families here have had to think about both states' rules on gas leasing.
intro: Friendsville is a small Susquehanna County borough near the New York border, founded originally by Quaker settlers, in a part of the dry-gas Marcellus fairway that's seen strong development from Cabot Oil & Gas, now Coterra Energy. Being this close to the state line occasionally raises questions for owners about whether New York's stricter drilling rules have any bearing here.
We buy mineral and royalty interests near Friendsville, whether producing under a Pennsylvania lease or held as a fractional family share.

sections.heading: Pennsylvania rules apply on the Pennsylvania side
paragraphs: New York has maintained a statewide ban on high-volume hydraulic fracturing since 2014, but that has no bearing on land in Pennsylvania — Susquehanna County acreage, including around Friendsville, is governed entirely by Pennsylvania law regardless of proximity to the border.

sections.heading: Strong dry-gas development in this corner of the county
paragraphs: Susquehanna County has been one of the most productive dry-gas counties in the play, and the Friendsville area has seen real development activity as part of that broader trend.

sections.heading: What we'll review
paragraphs: Lease terms, production history if any, and current activity nearby all factor into an offer.

Susquehanna County's Recorder of Deeds in Montrose is where we typically start pulling records for a Friendsville-area parcel. We'll also flag if any part of your documentation looks like it references a New York parcel by mistake, since border-area paperwork occasionally gets mixed up between the two states.

faqs.question: Does New York's fracking ban affect my Friendsville, PA mineral rights?
faqs.answer: No. New York's ban applies only to New York land. Pennsylvania acreage near Friendsville is governed by Pennsylvania law regardless of how close it sits to the state line.

faqs.question: Which operator is most active in Susquehanna County near Friendsville?
faqs.answer: Cabot Oil & Gas, now Coterra Energy, has been the dominant operator developing dry-gas Marcellus acreage across Susquehanna County, including this area.

faqs.question: Is Friendsville's Quaker settlement history relevant to mineral title?
faqs.answer: Not typically for current mineral rights, though very old deeds occasionally carry unusual language from early community land arrangements — we check the actual recorded chain regardless of settlement history.

faqs.question: Does being close to a state border ever complicate title work near Friendsville?
faqs.answer: Rarely for ownership itself, since Pennsylvania records govern Pennsylvania land regardless of border proximity, though we do occasionally see older deeds that reference boundary markers tied to the state line survey.
